overall: Observations as of ~10:45 PM PDT Saturday show temps cooling from a running max of 69.8°F, consistent with a marine-influenced overnight under mostly cloudy skies and patchy fog. Southwest onshore flow (3-5 mph) and elevated dewpoints near 62-63°F signal persistent marine layer influence that is likely to cap Sunday's afternoon high well below inland Heat Advisory values. Cooling velocity is active at roughly -1.8°F/hr, with the overnight low expected near 66°F per NWS.
forecast_obs_notes: NWS and the deterministic NWP guidance (GFS 76.6°F, HRRR 76.4°F, ECMWF 75.0°F) cluster around 75-77°F, but the NBM stands notably lower at 71.3°F, likely capturing cloud/fog suppression not fully resolved by the other models. The D1_NOW statistical model aligns more closely with NBM, assigning 59.1% probability to the 72-73°F even bucket and 45.8% to 74-75°F — a meaningful downward departure from raw NWP consensus that reflects the marine layer signal.
max_temp_prediction: With predominantly cloudy skies, patchy fog into the afternoon, and sustained onshore southwest flow, the marine layer looks well-positioned to suppress Sunday's peak significantly below the GFS/HRRR/NWS ~76°F target. The D1_NOW model's strong concentration around 72-73°F (59.1%) and NBM's 71.3°F both reinforce a cooler outcome. Confidence is moderately high that TMAX lands in the 72-74°F range, with the active even-bucket market top at 72-73°F representing the most probable single outcome; the 74-75°F bucket is the primary upside risk if cloud cover breaks earlier than forecast.
